tags: why do dogs bark at nothing
script: When your dog suddenly barks at what looks like an empty room, it's rarely actually nothing. Dogs hear frequencies up to about sixty five thousand hertz, while humans max out around twenty thousand, so they're picking up sounds you're simply not capable of hearing, a distant siren, another dog blocks away, even electrical hums from appliances. Their sense of smell is just as sharp, able to detect a person or animal that passed by minutes or even hours earlier. Barking at nothing can also be a territorial response to a subtle change, a shadow moving outside, a neighbor's door, or even their own reflection in a window at the right angle. So while it might look like your dog has lost it over an empty hallway, there's almost always a real trigger, it's just operating on a sensory level way beyond what you can perceive.
